analysis: Hash execution time by input size

classical_one_way_anova.interpretation: At alpha=0.05, reject the null hypothesis that all input-size group means are equal; evidence that at least one input-size group mean differs; this test does not identify which groups differ. Assumption diagnostics rejected residual normality and equal variance; treat this classical ANOVA result as nominal, not confirmatory.

residual_normality.test: Shapiro-Wilk on residuals centered within each size group

variance_homogeneity.test: Levene test centered on group medians

independence.note: The 30 observations per configuration are sequential repeated timings of the same input; temporal dependence cannot be assessed from the CSV.

anova_results_by_algorithm.assumption_status: Rejected diagnostic(s): residual normality, equal variance

alternative_test.name: Kruskal-Wallis
alternative_test.interpretation: At alpha=0.05, reject the null hypothesis that the input-size groups have the same rank distribution; evidence of a difference in rank distributions.
alternative_test.limitation: Kruskal-Wallis tests rank distributions rather than group means; it also assumes independent observations.

post_hoc.status: Not performed; standard Tukey HSD assumptions were not supported

analysis_method.throughput: input size in MiB divided by mean execution time in seconds
analysis_method.outlier_policy: No observations were removed, transformed, or winsorized.
analysis_method.anova_scope: Separate one-way ANOVA for each algorithm; input size is the five-level factor.
analysis_method.anova_interpretation_limit: A significant ANOVA indicates that at least one group mean differs; it does not identify which groups differ.
analysis_method.normality_test: Shapiro-Wilk test on within-group centered residuals.
analysis_method.plot: Median execution time with full observed minimum-to-maximum range; logarithmic axes.

limitations: The 30 timings in each configuration reuse one deterministic input and are sequential repeated measurements, not independent input samples.
Independence and temporal autocorrelation cannot be checked from the available CSV; classic ANOVA, Welch ANOVA, Kruskal-Wallis, and Tukey HSD all rely on independent observations.
The repeated 0-to-255 byte pattern controls content across algorithms but represents only one highly regular input pattern.
Algorithms and sizes are processed in a fixed order, so CPU load, frequency scaling, and thermal drift may confound comparisons.
The alpha threshold is applied separately to three algorithm-level ANOVAs; no cross-algorithm multiplicity correction is applied.
Statistical assumption tests diagnose distribution and variance, but do not repair dependence or other benchmark-design limitations.
